# Overview {#sec-02.0-section2 .unnumbered}

## Machine Learning

This section is an extensive exploration composed of four chapters, each one focused on a distinct aspect of machine learning techniques as applied to the modeling of infectious diseases. These machine learning models are designed with the broader scope of being utilized in transfer learning, enabling their application to diverse health data and other domains beyond infectious diseases.

### Chapter 5: Introduction to Machine Learning

This introductory chapter serves as a gateway to the world of machine learning within the context of infectious disease modeling. It offers a comprehensive overview, guiding readers through the fundamental concepts and methodologies. Starting from the basics of linear regression, the chapter progresses to more advanced techniques such as logistic regression. Through practical examples and case studies, readers gain a solid understanding of how machine learning can be leveraged to analyze and predict the spread of infectious diseases.

Additionally, this chapter provides a simple explanation of how to model fast-growing phenomena, such as the spread of infectious diseases. Conversely, it also looks at how a rapidly growing health impact can influence the health metrics of certain countries without significantly affecting the global perspective. More specifically, it examines the evolution of infection in specific countries and how this influences the overall level of health metrics.

### Chapter 6: Techniques for Machine Learning Applications

In this chapter, the focus shifts to the application of machine learning techniques in infectious disease modeling. Readers are introduced to a variety of advanced techniques aimed at refining models and optimizing performance. This includes an in-depth exploration of model adjustments such as feature engineering, resampling methods, and model selection strategies. By elucidating the nuances of when to utilize time series analysis versus logistic regression or random forests, readers are equipped with the tools to make informed modeling decisions.

### Chapter 7: Essential R Packages for Machine Learning

This chapter is dedicated to exploring the essential R packages tailored for machine learning applications in infectious disease modeling. From foundational packages like caret and tidymodels to specialized tools such as spdep and prophet, readers gain insights into the diverse array of resources available within the R ecosystem. Through hands-on tutorials and practical demonstrations, readers learn how to harness the power of these packages to streamline their modeling workflows and achieve meaningful insights.

### Chapter 8: Predictive Modeling and Beyond

The final chapter represents the culmination of the section, focusing on predictive modeling and its broader implications. Building upon the foundational knowledge acquired in previous chapters, readers delve into real-world case studies and predictive modeling exercises. By applying machine learning techniques to forecast disease trends, identify risk factors, and inform public health interventions, readers gain a deeper appreciation for the transformative potential of machine learning in infectious disease epidemiology.

> Engage critically with the material and explore the possibilities offered by machine learning.
